subject: Multiple concerns on a bifactor model

messages.author: 8f39ac5b920f9289
messages.subject: Multiple concerns on a bifactor model
parts:
Hi lavaan users,

I am trying to fit a bifactor model in lavaan with (1) two general factors (2) a mediator (defined as a latent with two indicators), and (3) several covariates (observed variables, e.g., gender, etc.). The model specification and the sem function code are below:

Bimodel <- "

# First general factor with four "group" factors
General1 =~ Pren_CESD1 + ... + Pren_pregn_anx_q4
G1_GroupF1 =~ Pren_CESD1 + ...
G1_GroupF2 =~ Pren_CESD3 + ...
G1_GroupF3 =~ Pren_CESD4_rec + ...
G1_GroupF4 =~ Pren_pregn_anx_q1 + ...

# Second general factor with three"group" factors
General2 =~ CBCL_emo_48m + ... + SDQ_peer_dad_60m
G2_GroupF1  =~ CBCL_emo_48m + ...
G2_GroupF2  =~ Dominic_sepanx + ...
G2_GroupF3  =~ SDQ_emo_dad_60m + ...
# Mediator
NE =~ 18m + 36m
# Four different covariates, such as gender, ethnicity, etc.
CV1 =~ 1*Gender 
CV2 =~ 1*Ethnicity
CV3 =~ 1*age_mom_yr 
CV4 =~ 1*Hamilton
Gender~~0*Gender 
Ethnicity~~0*Ethnicity
age_mom_yr~~0*age_mom_yr
Hamilton~~0*Hamilton
# Structural model: Direct effect
General2 ~ a*General1 + CV1 + CV2 + CV3 + CV4
# Mediator
NE ~ b*General1
General2 ~ c*NE
# Indirect effect
ac := b*c

# Total effect
total1 := a + (b*c)
"

FIT_Bi <- lavaan::sem(Bimodel, data, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", std.ov = TRUE, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal = T, meanstructure = TRUE)

I have four questions about the code, please share your wisdom!:
  • As you can see in the {sem} function above, I used "orthogonal=TRUE" and  "std.lv=TRUE" to make the factors orthogonal and to fix the variances of the factors to 1 (Reise, S. P., Moore, T. M., & Haviland, M. G., 2010). Is that correct?
  • Even though I used "meanstructure = TRUE", the outputs of "Latent Variables" don't show 1 values for each of the defined latent factors. I assume this is because I used "std.ov = TRUE", but is that correct?
  • Originally, I wanted to include four covarates as observed variables in the structural model specification, i.e., something like General2 ~ a*General1 + Gender + Ethnicity + age_mom_yr + Hamilton in the part of "# Structural model: Direct effect" above, but the model with this model specification did not converge and encountered error messages. Later, I found that people incorporate their covariates of interests as single-indicator latent variables, which is specified in the model above. Does this model specification make sense?? Here, the purpose of including those covariates is to see the effect of General1 on General2 after controlling for the covariates' effects on the variations of General2.
  • If I want to approximate fit indices and their cut-points using the Bollen-Stine Bootstrapping Method, how can I incorporate it into this model? I've been struggling with this issue because I also used "missing = "fiml" to impute some missing values in the dataset. 
Thank you so much for reading this long question. Thanks for your help in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple concerns on a bifactor model
parts: • As you can see in the {sem} function above, I used "orthogonal=TRUE" and  "std.lv=TRUE" to make the factors orthogonal and to fix the variances of the factors to 1 (Reise, S. P., Moore, T. M., & Haviland, M. G., 2010). Is that correct?

Yes, that is what those arguments do.  But note that for endogenous factors, you are setting the residual (not total) factor variance to 1.  It is just as arbitrary, and you can still find the standardized solution using summary(fit, std = TRUE) or standardizedSolution(fit)

• Even though I used "meanstructure = TRUE", the outputs of "Latent Variables" don't show 1 values for each of the defined latent factors. I assume this is because I used "std.ov = TRUE", but is that correct?

I'm not sure why you expect mean structure parameters to be 1.  But you should not standardize your observed variables.  Doing so without placing appropriate constraints on residual variances makes your SEs and test statistics invalid.  Leave that out, and you can still obtain the standardized solution after the model is fit.

• Originally, I wanted to include four covarates as observed variables in the structural model specification, i.e., something like General2 ~ a*General1 + Gender + Ethnicity + age_mom_yr + Hamilton in the part of "# Structural model: Direct effect" above, but the model with this model specification did not converge and encountered error messages. Later, I found that people incorporate their covariates of interests as single-indicator latent variables, which is specified in the model above. Does this model specification make sense?? Here, the purpose of including those covariates is to see the effect of General1 on General2 after controlling for the covariates' effects on the variations of General2.

That is what lavaan does already when you regress factors on observed variables.  To overcome convergence issues, you could consider setting conditional.x=TRUE, so that exogenous covariates are partialed out of modeled variables first, then the model is fitted to the residual covariance matrix.  This is computationally simpler, and might be advantageous.  However, it might be worth investigating why the convergence issues happen (e.g., multicollinearity?).

• If I want to approximate fit indices and their cut-points using the Bollen-Stine Bootstrapping Method, how can I incorporate it into this model? I've been struggling with this issue because I also used "missing = "fiml" to impute some missing values in the dataset.

FIML does not impute/replace missing values.  It simply utilizes all available information.  You can use bootstrapLRT() to obtain the Bollen-Stine p value for the chi-squared test, but you would have to program any model-based bootstrap of fit indices yourself.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
